$comment: CI gate: `check:bundle --budget scripts/bundle-budget.json --enforce`. eagerBytes caps the code evaluated at plugin startup and moduleActivationBytes caps what each module loads when it starts; outputBytes and stylesBytes are ratchets on main.js and styles.css. Lower a limit as code shrinks; never raise one without a recorded reason.
outputBudgetReason: T-16 Round 4: main.js measures 6863706B, +858B over the Round 3 limit 6862848B. The worktree also held concurrent non-T-16 (T-17) edits at measurement time, so the figure is not purely T-16; the T-16 part is the lazy progress lists, recorded-digest verification and one warning string pair in services/backup/import.ts and the lazy dictionary. Limit is the minimum 1KiB ceiling 6863872B; see the round4 section of CHG/evidence/T-16-budget-attribution.json. All lazy: the durable import progress record and per-step scoping, the real-codec definition check, `.backup` sidecar handling, effective-permission comparison and the completion-to-publish deferral. Eager, agent and notifications activation unchanged within limits; automations activation grows about 711B (to 220121B, limit 220160B) from the publish deferral/busy counter in core/service.ts and the codec check `checkAutomationDocument` in core/documents.ts (reached lazily through a one-line stub in automations api.ts). Full attribution is recorded in T-10 Evidence. T-15 (Round 3): main.js measures 6789098B. The growth over the previous 6758400B limit is the lazy recovery protocol (recovery-transaction/contracts/settings-recovery/app recovery), the legacy workbench import and its owners, strict drain/reload methods on SpaceService, workspace-store, stats, history and the automation registry, and the lazy migration dictionary.
